title: Jollof Rice
subtitle: West African tomato-braised rice with smoky depth
excerpt: Jollof rice is one of West Africa's great dishes: long-grain rice cooked directly in a blended tomato and pepper base so every grain takes on the flavour. The slightly scorched rice at the bottom of the pan, known as party jollof, is considered the best part. This recipe uses a Nigerian-style method.
sourceNotes: Jollof rice originated in the Wolof kingdoms of Senegal and The Gambia and spread across West and Central Africa over centuries. Each country has its own version, and the Nigerian versus Ghanaian debate is one of the most lively culinary arguments in the region.

content.text: The tomato base must be cooked until very dry and the oil separates before the rice goes in. Wet base means soggy jollof. Give it the full 20 minutes at step 3.

items.prepNote: rinsed until the water runs clear
1 roughly chopped for blending, 1 finely diced for frying

content.text: Blend the tinned tomatoes, red pepper, the roughly chopped onion, garlic, and ginger together until smooth. Set aside.
Heat the sunflower oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the finely diced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.

Pour in the blended tomato mixture. Add the paprika, cumin, thyme, and bay leaves. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20 minutes until the sauce has reduced and the oil separates from the top. The sauce needs to be very dry before the rice goes in.
Add the rinsed rice and stir to coat in the tomato base. Pour over the chicken stock and season generously with salt. Stir once, then cover tightly with foil and then the lid.
Cook over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid. The rice cooks by absorption and steam; lifting the lid extends the cooking time.
Remove from the heat, leave to rest with the lid on for 5 minutes, then uncover. Scatter the fresh coriander over the top and serve.

items.symptom: The rice has stuck firmly to the bottom
items.cause: The heat was too high or the pot was left on after the rice finished cooking
items.fix: A moderate scorch at the bottom is normal and desirable. If it has burned rather than scorched, add 2 tablespoons of water, replace the lid, and leave off the heat for 5 minutes to loosen it.

items.symptom: The rice is not cooked through after 30 minutes
items.cause: Not enough liquid, or the heat was too low
items.fix: Add 100 ml of hot water, replace the lid tightly, and cook for a further 10 minutes.
